added_provisions.reason: The proviso to Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (17) lets the parties authorise the notary in writing to dispense with the search. The map treated the search duty in rule (17)(a) as unqualified, so the exception was missing.

Companies Act s.185(2)(a) defines “major transaction” as an acquisition of assets worth more than half the value of the company's assets. PROV-M041-014 quotes only s.185(1), so the definition the answer turns on was cited by label but never quoted.

question_decisions.note: All 24 proposed provisions are real, verbatim and applicable at April 2023, and the corporate execution, major transaction, foreign shareholding and agricultural land ceiling chains hold up. The question is downgraded because five claims assert notarial duties the corpus does not impose: requiring the mortgage bond to be discharged, examining the vendor's earlier chain of deeds, and obtaining the company secretary's proof of shareholding. Those are conveyancing practice; the map's own corpus_gaps says such practice was to be excluded. Authority requirement is left at statute_only because the missing support is practice, not case law or Roman-Dutch doctrine, but a lawyer may prefer mixed_statute_and_case.

disagreements.researcher_position: The notary must require Mortgage Bond No. 2201 to be discharged or released before or at the transfer, and must call for the vendor's chain of deeds back to 1985, citing Notaries Ordinance s.31 rules (17)(a), (17)(b)(i) and (33) and Registration of Documents Ordinance s.7.
disagreements.verifier_position: Rules (17)(a) and (17)(b)(i) require the search and the certified folio extract; rule (33) requires best endeavours to obtain the title deed and endorse it; s.7 sets registration priority. None of them requires a discharge, and none requires a chain of deeds beyond the last registered entry. The steps are sound practice but not statutory duties on this corpus.

disagreements.researcher_position: The notary should obtain the company secretary's documentary proof that foreign shareholding is below fifty per cent, for the Registrar of Lands (Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act s.4(3)).
disagreements.verifier_position: Section 4(3) makes it the duty of the Registrar of Lands to satisfy himself by requiring the secretary to submit that proof. The Act imposes no corresponding duty on the notary.

disagreements.researcher_position: Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act s.3(1) is the charging provision for the duty the notary must see provided on the deed of transfer.
disagreements.verifier_position: Section 3 charges duty only on a “specified instrument”, and the closed list in s.4 does not include a transfer of immovable property; it could reach one only through a Ministerial Order under s.4(k), which is not in the corpus. The notarial duty in s.31 rule (6) stands on its own, but the charging chain does not close on this corpus.

unsupported_claims: CL-M041-Q01-015: no provision requires the notary to have a subsisting mortgage discharged or released.
CL-M041-Q01-016: the vendor's earlier chain of deeds has no statutory source; rule (33) reaches only “the title deed”.
CL-M041-Q01-021: s.4(3) of Act No. 38 of 2014 puts the proof requirement on the Registrar of Lands, not the notary.
CL-M041-Q01-024 and CL-M041-Q01-025: both conclusions carry the mortgage-discharge step forward.
temporal_issues: PROV-M041-010: rule (30A) was inserted by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(14), not by Act No. 47 of 2011 as the temporal note says; s.3 of the 2011 Act amended rule (26). The rule was in force at April 2023 either way.

PROV-M041-012: the closing words “shall be in force or avail in law unless” were substituted by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act, No. 30 of 2022, which the research notes do not mention; the map dated them to 1840. Section 2 was renumbered as subsection (1) only by Act No. 4 of 2024, so the “(1)” label is anachronistic for April 2023.

Corpus-wide: the s.31 body served by the corpus is the post-2024 consolidation. Every quoted rule was traced back to 31-2022 s.16 or to the untouched 1907 text, and none of the quoted words was introduced by 6-2024 s.3, so the excerpts hold at April 2023.
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (17) proviso, dispensing with the search on the parties' written authority — added as PROV-M041-901.
Companies Act s.185(2)(a), the definition of “major transaction” — added as PROV-M041-902.
Companies Act s.92(1) closing words, “such powers shall be exercised by special resolution”, are outside the quoted paragraph (b) in PROV-M041-015.

Land Reform Law s.66 excludes from “agricultural land” cultivated land owned by a public company on 29 May 1971 and certain religious and trust lands; the excerpt in PROV-M041-022 stops before those limbs. Immaterial here (a private company), but the definition also imports “private company” from the repealed Companies Ordinance.
Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act s.3 excepts s.2 and s.4(1) bars registration of a non-compliant instrument; neither is in the map, though neither changes the outcome on these facts.
Registration of Documents Ordinance s.7(1) opening words, identifying the instruments to which the voidness rule applies, are outside the excerpt in PROV-M041-023.
case_law_dependence: None. The gold answer cites no case and turns on no Roman-Dutch doctrine. The gap in the answer is untraced conveyancing practice, not judicial authority.
enrichment_issues: No statute name, section number or conclusion is leaked into the enriched background; the facts are stated as instructions and documents a notary would receive.

Each of the four synthetic_decisive facts (shareholding, shareholders' own agricultural holdings, the mortgage entry, the price against the company's assets) states why it is needed and what would change without it.

FACT-M041-Q01-006, the mortgage entry, is the only added fact whose stated effect (“a subsisting mortgage changes what the notary must do before the deed is drawn”) is not carried by any provision in the map; it drives the disputed claims.
The legal issue is unchanged: the question still asks what steps the notary must take on a purchase by a company.
duplicate_or_leak_issues: Ten of the twenty-four proposed provisions are separate rules of the same section, 1-1907/s31; that is how the Ordinance is drafted, not duplication, but a scorer keyed on section_id will see one section counted ten times.
M041-Q02 is Tier B and is correctly absent from the map.

lawyer_questions: Is a notary acting on a purchase under a legal duty to have a subsisting registered mortgage discharged or released before completion, or is that advice to the client rather than a notarial duty? The answer decides whether M041-Q01 can be a statute-only gold answer.

Should the customary examination of the vendor's chain of title, and the non-vesting certificate from the Land Reform Commission, be treated as part of a complete answer to “what steps should you take as the Notary”, and if so should the question be reclassified as mixed authority?
Is a deed of transfer of immovable property a “specified instrument” for the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act, and under which Order? The corpus list in s.4 does not reach it.
Does the Land Reform Law ceiling bite on the company itself as a “person” under s.66, in addition to the attribution to shareholders under s.8?
